mainTopic: Preparing foods, drinks and remedies on שבת: mustard, אֲלוּנְטִית, חלתית, and rubbing linen
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier point: an egg put into a mustard strainer on שבת is not בורר, because it is only there for color. Then the גמרא asks how mustard kneaded before שבת may be dissolved on שבת. רב, שמואל, רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן disagree about whether the hand, a utensil, both, or neither is allowed. Stories show scholars acting differently, and מר זוטרא rules that both ways are fine if one mixes gently and does not beat. The same rule applies to cress and garlic. Next, a ברייתא allows the spiced wine drink אֵנוֹמֵלִין on שבת but forbids אֲלוּנְטִית, a cooling drink used as a remedy. A new משנה then forbids soaking חלתית as medicine and forbids actively cleaning vetches and straw. The גמרא decides that soaking חלתית is only a rabbinic ban, and that soaking it in cold water is forbidden except when stopping a treatment already begun would be dangerous. The amud ends with stories about rubbing a linen shirt and a scarf on שבת, and רב חסדא begins a new statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The egg is only added for color
steps.stepSummary: This closes the earlier discussion about putting an egg into a mustard strainer. There is no problem of בורר, because the egg is only added to give the mustard color.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is only done to give color.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering why putting an egg into the mustard strainer on שבת is allowed. The answer is that the egg is only there to give the mustard a nice color.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that straining with the egg looks like בורר, separating one food from another. Since the egg is added only for color, nothing is really being picked out as waste, so it is not true selecting.

keyTerms.meaning: Color; here, the egg is used only to give the mustard color
The forbidden שבת labor of selecting or separating
Strainer; the mustard strainer from the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of an earlier discussion that started on the previous page. It is not connected to the mustard-dissolving dispute that begins right after it.

phrases.english: Because one does not do it
phrases.notes: "It" here means putting the egg into the mustard strainer.

phrases.english: except for color.
phrases.notes: The egg is only there for color, so this is not real selecting

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין אוֹתָהּ אֶלָּא לְגָוֶון
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier sugya from the previous page about the egg in the mustard strainer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the purpose of the act: it is for color, not for selecting
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Straining with an egg might count as בורר
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the egg is only for color, there is no real selection

steps.title: רב: dissolve kneaded mustard with a utensil, not by hand
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that mustard kneaded before שבת may be dissolved on שבת with a utensil, but not by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: mustard that someone kneaded before שבת, the next day (on שבת), רב said: he may dissolve it with a utensil but not by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a dispute about mustard that was already kneaded before שבת. רב says that on שבת you may mix it into liquid using a utensil, but not with your hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dissolving mustard looks like the labor of kneading (לש), so it must be done differently from the weekday way (a שינוי). רב holds that using a utensil is that change, so the hand is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Kneaded; also the name of the forbidden labor of kneading
He dissolves it, mixing it into liquid
Doing something in an unusual way, which can make it permitted on שבת

phrases.english: It was stated:
Mustard that one kneaded before Shabbat,
on the next day, Rav said:
He may dissolve it with a utensil
phrases.notes: רב sees the utensil as the change from the weekday way

phrases.english: but not by hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about mustard
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kneaded mustard may be dissolved on שבת with a utensil, not by hand

steps.title: שמואל objects: nobody dissolves mustard by hand on a weekday
steps.stepSummary: שמואל attacks רב's reasoning. On weekdays mustard is never dissolved by hand, because done that way it is fit only for donkeys. So the hand cannot be the normal method that must be avoided.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to him: Not by hand?! Do people dissolve it by hand every day?! That would be donkey food!
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל challenges רב. He points out that the hand is not the normal weekday method at all, so it makes no sense to forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that on שבת you must change from the normal weekday way. Mustard dissolved by hand comes out rough and lumpy, "donkey food," so the normal way must be with a utensil. That means רב has it backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? Introduces a challenging rhetorical question
Every day; on a regular weekday
Donkey food; something not fit for people

phrases.english: Shmuel said to him: (By hand?!)
phrases.notes: שמואל is asking why using your hand should be forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ כׇּל יוֹמָא בְּיָד מְמַחוּ לֵיהּ?!
phrases.english: Is that to say that every day they dissolve it by hand?!
It would be donkey food!
phrases.notes: Mustard dissolved by hand is not proper human food, so the hand is not the usual way

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל אַטּוּ כׇּל יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that using a utensil is the change and the hand is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The weekday method is a utensil, since hand-dissolved mustard is donkey food. So the hand is the change, not the utensil.

steps.title: שמואל's ruling: by hand yes, with a utensil no
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives the opposite ruling: dissolve the mustard by hand, which is the change, and not with a utensil, which is the normal weekday way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, שמואל said: He dissolves it by hand, and he does not dissolve it with a utensil.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רב's view, שמואל now gives his own ruling. It is the exact reverse of רב's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a change from the weekday method is needed. They only disagree about which method is the normal one. For שמואל the utensil is normal and so forbidden, while the hand is the permitted change.
steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל agree that a שינוי is needed. They argue only about which method counts as the change: רב says the utensil, שמואל says the hand.

phrases.english: Rather, Shmuel said:
He may dissolve it by hand
and he may not dissolve it with a utensil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב's ruling with the opposite one, based on the objection just raised
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kneaded mustard may be dissolved on שבת by hand, but not with a utensil

steps.title: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן: both forbidden or both permitted
steps.stepSummary: A second dispute. רבי אלעזר forbids dissolving mustard both by hand and with a utensil. רבי יוחנן permits both.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי אלעזר said: both this and that are forbidden. And רבי יוחנן said: both this and that are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another pair of אמוראים who argue about the same question. They do not split between hand and utensil: one forbids both methods and the other permits both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that neither method is a big enough change, so dissolving still counts as kneading. רבי יוחנן holds that since the mustard was already kneaded before שבת, dissolving it is permitted either way.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that; here, both by hand and with a utensil

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rabbi Elazar said:
Both this and that are forbidden.
phrases.notes: Both by hand and with a utensil

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Both this and that are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second dispute on the same case, with two more extreme positions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר forbids both methods; רבי יוחנן permits both

steps.title: אביי and רבא: the halacha is not like רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא both rule that the הלכה does not follow רבי יוחנן's lenient view that both methods are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both said: the הלכה is not like רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical ruling. אביי and רבא reject the most lenient view, that of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ruling against רבי יוחנן means you may not dissolve the mustard any way you like. At the least, some change from the normal method is needed, or it may be forbidden entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law does not follow

steps.whatToRemember: There are four opinions: רב (utensil only), שמואל (hand only), רבי אלעזר (both forbidden), and רבי יוחנן (both permitted). אביי and רבא rule against the lenient view of רבי יוחנן.
steps.confusionAlert: Saying the הלכה is "not like רבי יוחנן" does not tell us directly which of the other opinions we follow. It only rules out the view that both methods are permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: Ruling against רבי יוחנן is unusual, since the הלכה usually follows him. This sets up the next steps: once רבי יוחנן changes his position (step 7), אביי and רבא do rule like him (step 8).

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both said:
The halacha is not in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides against one side of the dispute in step 5
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The lenient view that both methods are permitted is rejected; dissolving kneaded mustard on שבת is not freely allowed

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר change their positions
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן switched to רבי אלעזר's strict view, and רבי אלעזר switched to שמואל's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן later took up the view of רבי אלעזר, forbidding both methods. רבי אלעזר took up the view of שמואל, allowing only by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that both אמוראים changed their minds about dissolving mustard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first רבי יוחנן allowed both methods and רבי אלעזר forbade both. Now רבי יוחנן forbids both, and רבי אלעזר allows dissolving by hand but not with a utensil, as שמואל said. This shift prepares the next step, where the הלכה is decided.

keyTerms.meaning: stood up, meaning he adopted or switched to a position
in the approach or opinion of

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the names. רבי יוחנן ends up strict (both forbidden). רבי אלעזר ends up following שמואל (by hand only).

phrases.aramaic: קָם רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּשִׁיטְתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan took up the position of Rabbi Elazar,
phrases.notes: He now forbids both by hand and with a utensil.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar took up the position of Shmuel.
phrases.notes: He now allows by hand but forbids a utensil.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָם רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּשִׁיטְתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Updates the positions in the dispute from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן now forbids both methods. רבי אלעזר follows שמואל and allows dissolving by hand only.

steps.title: אביי and רבא rule like רבי יוחנן's later view
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן's final position, which forbids both methods.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both said: the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא decide the הלכה like רבי יוחנן's new, strict position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits step 6. The הלכה does not follow רבי יוחנן's first, lenient view. It follows his later view, that mustard may not be dissolved by hand or with a utensil.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict step 6. Step 6 rejected רבי יוחנן's original lenient view. This step follows his later strict view.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both say:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan.
phrases.notes: That is, his later view, which forbids both methods.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the updated positions from step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Dissolving mustard on שבת is forbidden both by hand and with a utensil, following רבי יוחנן's later view.

steps.title: אביי would not eat mustard his mother prepared
steps.stepSummary: אביי's foster mother dissolved mustard for him on שבת, and he did not eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי's mother prepared mustard for him, and he did not eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing that אביי followed his strict ruling in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי had just ruled that both methods are forbidden. Refusing the mustard shows that he kept this ruling himself.

phrases.english: Abaye's mother prepared it for him,
phrases.notes: She dissolved mustard on שבת.

phrases.english: and he did not eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִימֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי עֲבַדָא לֵיהּ וְלָא אֲכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ruling of step 8 being followed in practice.
steps.raayaObject: The strict ruling of אביי and רבא.

steps.title: רב חייא בר אשי also refuses the mustard
steps.stepSummary: זעירא's wife prepared mustard for רב חייא בר אשי, and he did not eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירא's wife prepared mustard for רב חייא בר אשי, and he did not eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story shows another scholar following the strict practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חייא בר אשי was a student of זעירא. His refusal matches the strict ruling and sets up the wife's reaction in the next step.

phrases.english: Ze'eira's wife prepared it

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי, וְלָא אֲכַל.
phrases.english: for Rav Chiya bar Ashi, and he did not eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵיתְהוּ דִּזְעִירָא עֲבַדָא לֵיהּ לְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story of strict practice.

steps.title: The wife points out that his teacher ate it
steps.stepSummary: זעירא's wife challenges him: your teacher ate it, so why won't you?
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: I made it for your teacher and he ate it, and you won't eat it?
steps.whatsHappening: The wife questions his strictness, since his own teacher זעירא ate this mustard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her question shows that זעירא was lenient in practice. Great scholars behaved differently, so the strict ruling was not universally followed. This opens the way for the lenient evidence that comes next.

phrases.english: She said to him:
I made it for your teacher, and he ate it,
and you do not eat it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבָּךְ עֲבַדִי לֵיהּ וַאֲכַל וְאַתְּ לָא אָכְלַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the strict conduct in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The strict practice of רב חייא בר אשי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own teacher זעירא ate such mustard, which suggests it is permitted.

steps.title: רבינא ate mustard stirred with garlic
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר שבא saw people stir mustard for רבינא with the core of a garlic, and רבינא ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר שבא said: I was standing before רבינא, and they stirred mustard for him with the inner part of a garlic, and he ate it.
steps.whatsHappening: A third story shows a leading scholar eating mustard that was stirred on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stirring with a garlic core is an unusual tool, so it counts as a change from the normal way. רבינא ate it, which supports a more lenient practice.

keyTerms.meaning: the inner core of a garlic

phrases.english: Rava bar Shaba said:
I was standing before Ravina,
and they stirred it for him with the core of a garlic,
and he ate it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more evidence of lenient practice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבינא's conduct, as reported by רבא בר שבא.

steps.title: מר זוטרא rules: mustard may be mixed gently either way
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא rejects all the earlier opinions. Mustard kneaded before שבת may be dissolved by hand or with a utensil, and honey may be added, but it may only be mixed gently, not beaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: the הלכה does not follow any of these teachings. It follows this one: mustard kneaded on ערב שבת may be dissolved the next day by hand or with a utensil, and honey may be added. He may not beat it, only mix it.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives the final ruling. Both methods are allowed, as long as the mixing is gentle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the change had to come from the method (hand or utensil). מר זוטרא moves the change to the manner. Gentle mixing instead of forceful beating is enough.
steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: mustard kneaded before שבת may be dissolved by hand or with a utensil, but only with gentle mixing, not forceful beating.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line of the whole mustard discussion.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
The halacha does not follow any of these teachings,
but rather like this one that was stated:
Mustard that one kneaded on Shabbat eve,

phrases.aramaic: לְמָחָר מְמַחוֹ בֵּין בַּיָּד בֵּין בִּכְלִי
phrases.english: the next day he may dissolve it either by hand or with a utensil,
and he may put honey into it.
But he may not beat it; rather, he mixes it gently.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵית הִלְכְתָא כְּכׇל הָנֵי שְׁמַעְתָּתָא אֶלָּא כִּי הָא דְּאִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overrides all the earlier positions and stories.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both methods are allowed. The required change is gentle mixing instead of beating.

steps.title: The same rule for cress and garlic
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: cress or garlic prepared before שבת may have ingredients added the next day, but may only be mixed gently, not beaten or pounded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cress ground on ערב שבת: the next day he may add oil, vinegar, and אמיתא, but may not beat it, only mix. Garlic crushed on ערב שבת: the next day he may add beans and grits, but may not pound it, only mix, and he may add אמיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא that מר זוטרא quoted goes on to apply the same principle to two more dishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main work (grinding or crushing) was done before שבת. On שבת, adding ingredients and gently mixing is allowed. Forceful beating or pounding is not.

phrases.english: Cress that one ground on Shabbat eve,
the next day he may put oil and vinegar into it,
and add amita into it.
He may not beat it, but he mixes it.
Garlic that one crushed on Shabbat eve,
the next day he may put beans and grits into it,
and he may not pound it, but he mixes it,
and he may add amita into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food processed before שבת may have ingredients added on שבת with gentle mixing, but not forceful beating or pounding.

steps.title: What is אמיתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word אמיתא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is אמיתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain an unfamiliar word from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple vocabulary question, not a challenge. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: an herb named in the ברייתא

phrases.english: What is amita?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word used in step 14.

steps.title: אמיתא is mint
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אמיתא is mint.
steps.simpleTranslation: Mint.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines the word: it means mint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא is clear: mint may be added to cress and garlic dishes on שבת.

phrases.english: Mint.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15.

steps.title: אביי learns that mint is good for cress
steps.stepSummary: אביי infers from the ברייתא that adding mint is beneficial for cress.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: learn from this that mint is good for cress.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a practical lesson from the ברייתא's instruction to add mint to cress.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells us to add mint to cress, so mint must improve the dish. This is a side point about food, not a new ruling of הלכה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ הַאי נִינְיָיא מְעַלְּיָא לְתַחְלֵי.
phrases.english: Learn from this that mint is beneficial for cress.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ הַאי נִינְיָיא מְעַלְּיָא לְתַחְלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the definition in step 16.

steps.title: אֵנוֹמֵלִין is allowed on שבת but אֲלוּנְטִית is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line allowing אֵנוֹמֵלִין and brings a ברייתא that allows it but forbids אֲלוּנְטִית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one may prepare אֵנוֹמֵלִין on שבת.' The רבנן taught in a ברייתא: One may prepare אֵנוֹמֵלִין on שבת, but one may not prepare אֲלוּנְטִית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא about it. The ברייתא adds a second drink that is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only told us that אֵנוֹמֵלִין is allowed. The ברייתא adds a contrast: a similar wine drink, אֲלוּנְטִית, is forbidden. We do not yet know why. The next steps explain what each drink is.

keyTerms.meaning: A spiced wine drink made of wine, honey and pepper
A cooling wine drink used after the bathhouse

phrases.english: And one may prepare anumlin on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may prepare anumlin on Shabbat,
but one may not prepare aluntit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the mustard and cress discussion to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אֵנוֹמֵלִין may be prepared on שבת; אֲלוּנְטִית may not.

steps.title: What are these two drinks?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what אֵנוֹמֵלִין and אֲלוּנְטִית actually are.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is אֵנוֹמֵלִין, and what is אֲלוּנְטִית?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a simple clarifying question. It is setting up the definitions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two drinks sound alike, since both are wine mixtures. To understand why one is allowed and one is forbidden, we must know what goes into each.

keyTerms.meaning: And which one is it? (a request for a definition)

phrases.english: And what is anumlin,
and what is aluntit?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא אֵנוֹמֵלִין וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא אֲלוּנְטִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for definitions of the two terms in the ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The ingredients and purpose of each drink.

steps.title: אֵנוֹמֵלִין is a spiced drink; אֲלוּנְטִית is a cooling drink for after the bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: אֵנוֹמֵלִין is wine, honey and pepper. אֲלוּנְטִית is aged wine, clear water and balsam, drunk after the bathhouse to cool down.
steps.simpleTranslation: אֵנוֹמֵלִין is wine, honey and pepper. אֲלוּנְטִית is aged wine, clear water and balsam, which people make for the bathhouse, to cool off.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא defines both drinks. This shows why one is allowed and the other is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אֵנוֹמֵלִין is an ordinary tasty drink, so making it is normal food preparation. אֲלוּנְטִית is made to treat the body after the heat of the bathhouse. That makes it רפואה (healing), which the רבנן forbade on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: Both drinks are wine mixtures. The difference is not the wine itself but the purpose: one is for enjoyment, the other is for healing.

phrases.english: Anumlin is wine, honey, and pepper.
Aluntit is aged wine
and clear water and balsam,
which they make for the bathhouse, to cool down.
phrases.notes: Its use as a remedy is why it is forbidden on שבת

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of definitions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אֵנוֹמֵלִין is a regular spiced drink. אֲלוּנְטִית is a cooling, healing drink for after the bathhouse.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the general rule: preparing food or drink is fine on שבת, but preparing something mainly as a remedy is forbidden.

steps.title: רב יוסף describes how strong aluntit was
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tells how one cup of this drink from מר עוקבא chilled him from head to toe. He feared a second cup would use up his reward in the World to Come.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Once I went after מר עוקבא into the bathhouse. When I came out, he gave me one cup of this wine to drink. I felt it from the hair on my head to the nails of my feet. If he had given me another cup, I was afraid it would be taken off my merit for the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tells a personal story to show how powerful אֲלוּנְטִית is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story proves that אֲלוּנְטִית has a strong effect on the body. That supports calling it רפואה. A second cup could have been dangerous for him. If he had survived it, that rescue would have been taken off his merit for the World to Come.

keyTerms.meaning: Merit for the World to Come

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
One time I went in
after Mar Ukva into the bathhouse.
When I came out, he came
and gave me one cup of wine to drink,
and I felt it from the hair of my head
down to the nails of my feet.
And if he had given me another cup to drink,
I would have been afraid that perhaps
they would deduct it from my merit in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: זִימְנָא חֲדָא עַלִּית בָּתַר מָר עוּקְבָא לְבֵי בָאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows from real life how strong the drink defined in the ברייתא is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אֲלוּנְטִית has a powerful effect on the body.

steps.title: But מר עוקבא drank it every day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if one cup was so overwhelming, how did מר עוקבא drink it daily?
steps.simpleTranslation: But מר עוקבא drank it every day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יוסף's story by pointing to מר עוקבא's habit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a second cup was too much for רב יוסף, then daily drinking should also have been too much for מר עוקבא. Either the drink is not so strong, or something about מר עוקבא is different.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מָר עוּקְבָא דְּשָׁתֵי כׇּל יוֹמָא?
phrases.english: But Mar Ukva drank it every day?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מָר עוּקְבָא דְּשָׁתֵי כׇּל יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story just told.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the drink was overwhelming
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מר עוקבא drank it daily without harm, which seems to contradict how strong רב יוסף said it was.

steps.title: מר עוקבא was used to it
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא was different because he had grown used to the drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא is different, because he was used to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that daily habit made the drink easy for מר עוקבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The drink really is strong, as רב יוסף said. Someone who drinks it regularly gets used to it, so it no longer overwhelms him.

keyTerms.meaning: Was used to it (literally, 'tread on it' often)

phrases.english: Mar Ukva is different, since he was accustomed to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the person: habit changes the effect.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Daily drinking by מר עוקבא shows the drink is not so strong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The drink is strong; מר עוקבא was simply used to it.
steps.whatToRemember: אֲלוּנְטִית is forbidden on שבת because it is a healing drink, and the story shows how strong it is. מר עוקבא could handle it only because he was used to it.

steps.title: New משנה: soaking asafoetida and cleaning vetches
steps.stepSummary: One may not soak חִילְתִּית in lukewarm water but may put it in vinegar. One may not soak or rub כַּרְשִׁינִין to clean them but may put them in a sieve or basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not soak חִילְתִּית in lukewarm water, but one may put it into vinegar. One may not soak vetches in water or rub them, but one may put them into a sieve or a basket.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with two cases about preparing things on שבת. Each case has a forbidden way and an allowed way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soaking חִילְתִּית in lukewarm water makes a medicine, so it is forbidden as רפואה. Putting it in vinegar is normal cooking use, so it is allowed. Soaking or rubbing vetches is done to remove the chaff, which is like separating work. Simply putting them in a sieve or basket is allowed even if some chaff falls off, because that is not the goal.

keyTerms.meaning: Vetches, a kind of legume used mostly as animal feed
Rub by hand to remove the husks

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may not soak asafoetida in lukewarm water,
phrases.notes: This makes a medicinal drink

phrases.english: but one may place it into vinegar.
phrases.notes: Normal use as a seasoning

phrases.english: And one may not soak vetches in water to clean them
nor rub them by hand,
but one may place them into a sieve
or into a basket.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין שׁוֹרִין אֶת הַחִילְתִּית בְּפוֹשְׁרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It continues the theme of healing preparations and adds the theme of separating.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A medicinal soak is forbidden but ordinary food use is allowed. Actively cleaning vetches is forbidden, but simply placing them in a sieve or basket is allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: Putting vetches into a sieve is allowed even though the sieve is a separating tool. The difference is that one is just putting them there, not shaking or sifting.

steps.title: משנה: sifting straw versus carrying it in a sieve
steps.stepSummary: One may not sift straw in a sieve or put it up high so the wind blows the chaff away. One may carry it in a sieve and pour it into the animal's trough.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not sift straw in a sieve. Nor may one put it on a high place so that the chaff will fall away. But one may take it in a sieve and put it into the feeding trough.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a third case, about straw for animals. Again it gives forbidden ways and an allowed way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sifting straw in a sieve is like the forbidden work of separating. Putting it up high so the wind removes the chaff is like winnowing. Carrying it in a sieve just to bring it to the trough is allowed, even if some chaff falls out, because the goal is moving it, not cleaning it.

keyTerms.meaning: Chaff, the light waste that blows away

phrases.english: One may not sift straw in a sieve,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יִתְּנֶנּוּ עַל גַּבֵּי מָקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ
phrases.english: and one may not place it on a high place
so that the chaff will fall away.
phrases.notes: Similar to winnowing in the wind

phrases.english: But he may take it in a sieve
and place it into the trough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with another case of separating that is forbidden when done on purpose and allowed when it happens along the way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Deliberately removing chaff from straw is forbidden. Carrying straw in a sieve to the trough is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: The common thread in this משנה is intent. Actively cleaning or making medicine is forbidden on שבת. Ordinary use, where some cleaning happens by itself, is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea for the coming discussion: the same tool, a sieve, can be forbidden or allowed depending on how and why it is used.

steps.title: What if someone already soaked the חלתית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the law is if someone has already soaked חלתית on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The question was asked: if someone soaked it, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה with a question. The משנה said not to soak חלתית, and now we ask what happens if someone already did. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only gave the rule before the act: 'don't soak.' The גמרא wants to know how serious it is after the act. Is it a real Torah-level מלאכה that requires a חטאת, or something lighter?

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and analyzes the משנה
A question was raised before them (the scholars)
He soaked (past tense; it was already done)

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא on this משנה

phrases.english: A question was raised before them: if he soaked it, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Refers to soaking חלתית, the topic of the משנה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה rule about חלתית quoted in Step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the status of someone who has already soaked חלתית on שבת? Is he liable for a חטאת?

steps.title: רב אדא says he must bring a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא נרשאה explains, in front of רב יוסף, that someone who soaked it is liable for a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא of נרש explained before רב יוסף: if he soaked it, he is liable for a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא נרשאה answers the question. He says soaking חלתית is a full Torah-level act, so the person must bring a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is only brought for doing a Torah-level מלאכה by mistake. So רב אדא is treating soaking as a real מלאכה, probably like cooking. This strong position is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable to bring a sin-offering (for an accidental Torah-level violation)

phrases.english: Rav Adda of Naresh explained it
phrases.notes: נרשאה just means he was from the town of נרש.

phrases.english: before Rav Yosef:
If he soaked it, he is liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמָא רַב אַדָּא נַרְשָׁאָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Soaking חלתית is a Torah-level act; one who does it by mistake brings a חטאת.

steps.title: אביי: then soaking meat in water would also make you liable
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב אדא: if soaking makes you liable, then soaking meat in water would too, which is absurd.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, if someone soaked meat in water, would he also be liable?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב אדא's answer. He shows that it leads to a ridiculous result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soaking meat in plain water does nothing like cooking, and nobody would say it is a מלאכה. If soaking חלתית were a Torah-level מלאכה just because it is soaking, the same would apply to meat. Since that is clearly wrong, soaking alone cannot be a Torah-level violation.

keyTerms.meaning: But if that is so... (introduces an absurd result)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But if that is so, if one soaked meat in water,
would he also be liable?
phrases.notes: He's not really asking; he means: surely not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא's ruling that soaking חלתית requires a חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: by the same logic, soaking meat in water would be a מלאכה, which is plainly false.

steps.title: אביי: it is only a rabbinic ban on weekday behavior
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives his own answer: soaking חלתית is forbidden only מדרבנן, so that a person does not act on שבת as he does on weekdays.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: It is forbidden by rabbinic law, so that he will not do it the way he does on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי replaces רב אדא's answer with his own. There is no חטאת. The ban is a rabbinic rule meant to keep שבת different from the week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether the act is Torah-level or not. אביי says it is not. The חכמים banned it because soaking חלתית is a normal weekday preparation, and doing it on שבת makes שבת feel like a regular day. So someone who did it does not bring a חטאת.
steps.whatToRemember: Soaking חלתית does not require a חטאת. It is only a rabbinic ban, so that one does not treat שבת like a weekday.
steps.confusionAlert: This step is not saying soaking חלתית is allowed. It is still forbidden. The only change is the level: it is rabbinic, not Torah-level, so there is no חטאת.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said: It is prohibited by rabbinic law,
so that he should not act in the manner
that he acts during the week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רב אדא in Step 28, אביי gives a new answer to the question of Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No חטאת; the ban is only rabbinic, to prevent weekday-style conduct on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן asks about soaking חלתית in cold water
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks רבי ינאי whether one may soak חלתית in cold water on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן asked רבי ינאי: May one soak חלתית in cold water?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question starts. רבי יוחנן wants to know if the ban covers cold water too. This sets up רבי ינאי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (Step 24) only mentioned lukewarm water. So it is unclear whether cold water is allowed or also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Asafoetida, a plant resin used as medicine and spice

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan asked Rabbi Yannai:
What is the law about soaking asafoetida in cold water?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about cold water, separate from the חטאת question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is soaking חלתית in cold water allowed on שבת?

steps.title: רבי ינאי: it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי answers that soaking in cold water is also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי gives a short, clear answer: cold water is forbidden too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer seems to go against the wording of the משנה. That sets up רבי יוחנן's challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is prohibited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Soaking חלתית in cold water is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the משנה implies cold water is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges with a דיוק from the משנה: it forbids lukewarm water, which implies cold water is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: One may not soak חלתית in lukewarm water. This implies that in cold water it is allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes back on רבי ינאי using the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה wanted to ban all water, why mention lukewarm? Naming lukewarm water suggests cold water is fine. That contradicts רבי ינאי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
One may not soak asafoetida in lukewarm water,
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה (see Step 24)

phrases.english: which implies that in cold water it is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 31 using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's ruling that cold water is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inference from the משנה's wording: forbidding only lukewarm implies cold is permitted.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: the משנה is a lone opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי answers that this is the difference between his understanding and רבי יוחנן's: the משנה follows a single opinion that we do not follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, what is the difference between me and you? The משנה is the opinion of a single תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי defends his ruling. He says the משנה reflects one individual's view, not the main הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי agrees the משנה implies cold water is allowed. But he says that משנה follows only one תנא, and the majority disagrees. So his ruling stands. He hints that knowing this is what makes him the teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between me and you? (I know more than the plain text)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ינאי is not saying the משנה is wrongly written. He is saying it is accurate, but it follows a minority view, so we don't rule like it.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
what is the difference between me and you?
phrases.notes: My deeper knowledge is that I know the משנה is a minority view

phrases.english: The mishna is an individual opinion,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן מַה בֵּין לִי וְלָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a minority opinion (יחידאה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's wording means cold water is permitted according to the accepted הלכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows a lone view; the accepted view forbids cold water too.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא: the חכמים forbid both, רבי יוסי allows cold
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי proves his point from a ברייתא: the first opinion forbids hot and cold water, and only רבי יוסי allows cold.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: One may not soak חלתית in hot water or in cold water. רבי יוסי says: In hot water it is forbidden; in cold water it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי brings a ברייתא to show that allowing cold water is only רבי יוסי's view. The main view forbids both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows two opinions. The unnamed first view (the majority) forbids all water, and רבי יוסי alone allows cold water. So the משנה, which implies cold is fine, follows רבי יוסי. רבי ינאי rules like the majority.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה that only bans lukewarm water follows רבי יוסי. The majority forbids soaking חלתית in both hot and cold water, and רבי ינאי rules like them.

phrases.english: as it was taught:
One may not soak asafoetida
neither in hot water nor in cold water.
Rabbi Yosei says: In hot water it is prohibited;
in cold water it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim of Step 33 that the משנה is a lone view.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה follows an individual opinion (רבי יוסי) and the majority forbids cold water.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the majority view forbidding both hot and cold, against רבי יוסי who permits cold.

steps.title: What is soaked asafoetida used for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what purpose soaked חלתית serves.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what is it made?
steps.whatsHappening: After the debate about soaking חלתית, the גמרא pauses to ask a basic question: what do people use it for? This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we only knew that people soak חלתית. Knowing its use matters, because it tells us whether this counts as medicine on שבת. The answer will also lead into a real-life case.

keyTerms.meaning: Do they make or prepare it

phrases.english: For what do they prepare it?
phrases.notes: Refers to the soaked חלתית discussed above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the halachic debate to clarifying the practical purpose of חלתית.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The medical or practical use of soaked חלתית.

steps.title: It treats heaviness of the heart
steps.stepSummary: חלתית is used for heaviness of the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: For heaviness of the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that people drink it to relieve a heavy, pained feeling in the heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that חלתית has a healing use. That raises the concern of medicine on שבת, which the next steps will address.

keyTerms.meaning: Heaviness of the heart, a kind of chest or heart pain

phrases.english: For heaviness of the heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a remedy for heaviness of the heart.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יוסף's three-day treatment
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יוסף is told to drink חלתית over three days. He drinks on Thursday and Friday and then asks the בית המדרש about שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יוסף suffered from heaviness of the heart. He came before מר עוקבא, who told him: go drink three shekels' weight of חלתית over three days. He drank on Thursday and on Friday. In the morning, on שבת, he went and asked in the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real story to set up a שבת question. The third day of the treatment falls on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail that he already drank on two days is important. It will later explain why stopping on שבת would be dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: Shekels, used here as units of weight
The fifth day of the week, Thursday

steps.confusionAlert: Remember that he already drank on Thursday and Friday. The גמרא will use this fact in step 42.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יוֹסֵף חָשׁ בְּיוּקְרָא דְלִיבָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yosef felt heaviness of the heart.
He came before Mar Ukva.
He said to him: Go drink
three shekels' weight of asafoetida over three days.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל אִישְׁתִּי חַמְשָׁא בְּשַׁבְּתָא וּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא.
phrases.english: He went and drank on Thursday and on Shabbat eve.
In the morning, he went and asked in the study hall.
phrases.notes: The morning of שבת, the third day of the treatment.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יוֹסֵף חָשׁ בְּיוּקְרָא דְלִיבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case of using חלתית for heaviness of the heart.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A narrative setup: the treatment's third day falls on שבת, which raises a halachic question.

steps.title: Drinking חלתית on שבת is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The בית המדרש cites a ברייתא: a person may drink even a קב or two of it without concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told him: the school of רב אדא taught (some say the school of מר בר רב אדא): A person may drink a קב or two קבין and need not be concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars answer that drinking חלתית on שבת is allowed, even in large amounts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual concern is the rabbinic ban on taking medicine on שבת. Healthy people also drink חלתית, so drinking it does not look like medicine, and there is no worry.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַב אַדָּא,
phrases.english: They said to him: The school of Rav Adda taught,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ תָּנָא דְּבֵי מָר בַּר רַב אַדָּא:
phrases.english: and some say the school of Mar bar Rav Adda taught:
A person may drink a kav or two kav
phrases.notes: Even this large amount is allowed.

phrases.english: and he need not be concerned.
phrases.notes: No concern about the ban on medicine on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַב אַדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question he brought to the בית המדרש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Drinking חלתית on שבת is permitted, even in large amounts.

steps.title: The real question: soaking, not drinking
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא clarifies that his doubt is about soaking the חלתית, not about drinking it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I have no question about drinking. My question is about soaking. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא tells them they answered the wrong question. He needs to know whether he may soak the חלתית on שבת so that it can be drunk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties the story back to the earlier debate in steps 30-34. There the first opinion forbids soaking even in cold water, and only רבי יוסי allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: I have no question about it

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לִשְׁתּוֹת — לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לִי,
phrases.english: He said to them: About drinking, I have no question.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי — לִשְׁרוֹת, מַאי?
phrases.english: What I am asking about is soaking. What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: לִשְׁתּוֹת לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לִי, כִּי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the scope of the question answered in step 38.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may soak חלתית on שבת.

steps.title: רב rules: soak in cold water and set in the sun
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין reports that רב הונא, quoting רב, permits soaking in cold water and then placing it in the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין told them: This happened to me. I asked רב אדא בר אהבה, and he had no answer. I asked רב הונא, and he said: This is what רב says: one soaks it in cold water and places it in the sun.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone who faced the same case reports a ruling from רב: soaking in cold water is allowed, and the sun may warm it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hot water is avoided, but cold water followed by the sun's heat is permitted. Warming something with the sun is not cooking.

keyTerms.meaning: It happened to me, a personal incident
He did not have it in hand, meaning he had no answer

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Avin said to them:
There was such an incident with me,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתַאי שְׁאֵילְתֵּיהּ לְרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
phrases.english: and I came and asked it of Rav Adda bar Ahava,
and he did not have an answer.
I came and asked Rav Huna, and he said:
This is what Rav says:
One soaks it in cold water and places it in the sun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the soaking question of step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רב, one may soak חלתית in cold water and set it in the sun.

steps.title: Does רב follow the lenient minority?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב's ruling follows the opinion that permits cold-water soaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this like the one who permits?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that רב's ruling sounds like רבי יוסי's lone opinion. רבי ינאי said earlier that we do not follow that opinion. The next step will answer this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 34 the first opinion forbade soaking even in cold water. If רב permits it, he seems to side with the minority, which is a problem.

phrases.english: Is it according to the one who permits?
phrases.notes: That is, רבי יוסי, who allows cold-water soaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב's ruling against the ברייתא brought in step 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב's ruling depends on the minority view of רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Even the strict view permits here because of danger
steps.stepSummary: Even the opinion that forbids would allow soaking here. He already began the treatment, and stopping would endanger him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to the one who forbids: that applies only where he had not drunk at all. But here, since he drank on Thursday and Friday, if he does not drink on שבת he will be in danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב does not have to follow the minority. In this particular case, everyone would agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on cold-water soaking applies to a normal case. Once someone has started the three-day course, stopping is dangerous, and danger to life overrides the rabbinic ban.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who forbids
These words apply only (to a limited case)

steps.whatToRemember: רב's lenient ruling is not a ruling like רבי יוסי. It is a special exception: once the treatment has begun, stopping it is dangerous, so even the strict opinion permits soaking.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the general ruling against cold-water soaking in place, while showing how danger to health creates an exception.

phrases.english: Even according to the one who forbids:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא אִישְׁתִּי כְּלָל,
phrases.english: that applies only where he had not drunk at all,
but here, since he drank
on Thursday and Shabbat eve,
if he does not drink on Shabbat, he will be endangered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 41 by limiting the strict view to an ordinary case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the prohibition (an exception because of danger)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב must hold like רבי יוסי, the rejected minority.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the strict view permits here, because stopping a treatment already begun is dangerous.

steps.title: רב אחא is brought to רב ספרא's house
steps.stepSummary: Leaning on his nephew רב נחמן בר יצחק, רב אחא asks to be brought into רב ספרא's house, and he is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יוסף was walking, leaning on the shoulder of רב נחמן בר יצחק, his sister's son. He said to him: when we reach רב ספרא's house, bring me in. When they arrived, he brought him in.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story about רב אחא begins. This step sets up a new question he will ask רב ספרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a separate topic about laundry and whitening on שבת. It is linked to the previous section only by the same main character.

phrases.aramaic: מִיסְתְּמִיךְ וְאָזֵיל רַב אַחָא בַּר יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yosef was walking, leaning

phrases.aramaic: אַכַּתְפֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק בַּר אֲחָתֵיהּ.
phrases.english: on the shoulder of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, his sister's son.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי מָטֵינַן לְבֵי רַב סָפְרָא עַיְּילִינַּן.
phrases.english: He said to him: When we reach Rav Safra's house, bring me in.
When they arrived, he brought him in.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיסְתְּמִיךְ וְאָזֵיל רַב אַחָא בַּר יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story with the same main character, which opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A narrative setup for the question about the linen shirt.

steps.title: May one rub a stiff linen shirt on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא asks whether rubbing a linen shirt on שבת is softening, which is allowed, or whitening, which is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked him: May one rub a linen shirt on שבת? Is his intent to soften it, which is allowed? Or perhaps his intent is to whiten it, which is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא asks about rubbing a freshly laundered, stiff linen shirt. The question depends on what the person intends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a garment whiter is a form of laundering, which is forbidden on שבת. Simply making it soft is not. The question is which purpose the rubbing serves.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ: מַהוּ לְכַסְכּוֹסֵי כִּיתָּנִיתָא בְּשַׁבְּתָא?
phrases.english: He asked him: What is the law about rubbing a linen shirt on Shabbat?

phrases.aramaic: לְרַכּוֹכֵי כִּיתָּנִיתָא קָא מִיכַּוֵּין — וְשַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: Does he intend to soften the shirt, so it is fine?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא לְאוֹלוֹדֵי חִיוָּרָא קָמִיכַּוֵּין — וַאֲסִיר?
phrases.english: Or perhaps he intends to produce whiteness, so it is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ: מַהוּ לְכַסְכּוֹסֵי כִּיתָּנִיתָא בְּשַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The question that the visit in step 43 was leading up to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether rubbing a linen shirt counts as softening (permitted) or whitening (forbidden).

steps.title: It is softening, so it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא rules that the intent is to soften, so it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: His intent is to soften, and it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא answers that people rub the shirt only to make it soft, so it is allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the normal purpose of rubbing is softening and not whitening, the act is not treated as laundering. The person's ordinary intent decides the law.
steps.whatToRemember: Rubbing a stiff linen shirt on שבת is permitted, because the purpose is softening, not whitening.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְרַכּוֹכֵי קָא מִיכַּוֵּין וְשַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: He said to him: He intends to soften, and it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 44.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The intent is softening, so rubbing a linen shirt on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: The nephew asks what was asked
steps.stepSummary: When רב אחא comes out, רב נחמן בר יצחק asks him what question he put to רב ספרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came out, he said to him: What did the master ask him?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. רב אחא leaves רב ספרא's house, and his nephew asks what the question was. This sets up the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the question from steps 44-45. Now the גמרא retells it through the nephew's conversation. This opens the door for the nephew to push further.

phrases.english: When he went out and came,
phrases.notes: רב אחא leaving רב ספרא's house

phrases.english: he said to him:
phrases.notes: רב נחמן בר יצחק speaks to רב אחא

phrases.english: What did the master ask of him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after רב ספרא's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What question רב אחא asked רב ספרא.

steps.title: רב אחא reports the question and the permission
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא says he asked about rubbing a linen shirt on שבת and was told it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I asked him, what is the law about rubbing a linen shirt on שבת? And he told me: it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא answers his nephew. He asked about rubbing a linen shirt on שבת, and רב ספרא said it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rubbing (כסכוס) softens the linen. Since the purpose is softening and not whitening, it is not treated as laundering. This repeats the ruling from step 45 so the nephew can question it.

phrases.english: He said to him: I asked of him:
What is the law about rubbing a linen shirt on Shabbat,
and he said to me: It is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the nephew's question from step 46.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question was about rubbing a linen shirt on שבת, and רב ספרא permitted it.

steps.title: Why not ask about a scarf too?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks why רב אחא didn't also ask about rubbing a scarf.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let the master ask about a scarf?
steps.whatsHappening: The nephew wonders why the question was only about a shirt. A scarf is also cloth that people rub, so why not ask about it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nephew is trying to understand the full scope of the question. If shirts are uncertain, scarves seem just as uncertain. This sets up רב אחא's explanation.

phrases.english: And let the master ask about a scarf?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the inquiry was limited to a shirt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב אחא did not also ask about a scarf.

steps.title: The scarf was already settled by רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא explains that he had already asked רב הונא about a scarf, and רב הונא permitted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: I don't need to ask about a scarf, because I asked רב הונא and he resolved it for me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא says the scarf question was already answered. רב הונא told him it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the scarf case was clear to him and only the shirt was in doubt. That raises the next question: if a scarf is permitted, why wasn't the shirt obviously permitted too?

keyTerms.meaning: I have a question / I am uncertain

phrases.english: About a scarf I have no question,
because I asked Rav Huna
and he resolved it for me.
phrases.notes: He ruled that it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the scarf was not asked about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא had already permitted rubbing a scarf.

steps.title: Then learn the shirt from the scarf
steps.stepSummary: The nephew challenges him: if a scarf is permitted, that should settle the shirt question too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the master resolve it from the scarf!
steps.whatsHappening: The nephew pushes back. If rubbing a scarf is permitted, why was רב אחא unsure about a shirt? Just apply the same answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes a shirt and a scarf are the same case, since both are linen rubbed to soften it. If so, רב אחא's question to רב ספרא was unnecessary.

phrases.english: And let the master resolve it from the scarf?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer from step 49 to challenge the need for the question in step 47.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא's uncertainty about the shirt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A scarf and a shirt seem identical, so רב הונא's permission for the scarf should already cover the shirt.

steps.title: A shirt looks like whitening, a scarf does not
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא distinguishes the cases: rubbing a shirt looks like making it white, while rubbing a scarf does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, it looks like making it white. Here, it does not look like making it white.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא explains why the scarf didn't settle the shirt. People care how white a shirt is, so rubbing it looks like laundering. With a scarf, nobody thinks you are whitening it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whitening (ליבון) is a forbidden form of laundering on שבת. With a shirt there is real room to suspect whitening, so the shirt question needed its own ruling. With a scarf the intent is clearly only softening.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'הָתָם' (there) refers to the shirt, and 'הָכָא' (here) refers to the scarf, following one explanation. Don't flip them. The shirt is the one that looks like whitening, which is exactly why it needed its own question.
steps.whatToRemember: A scarf was clearly permitted because rubbing it doesn't look like whitening. A shirt needed its own ruling because it does look like whitening. רב ספרא still permitted it, since the intent is to soften.

phrases.english: He said to him:
There, it looks like generating whiteness,
phrases.notes: The shirt

phrases.english: here, it does not look like generating whiteness.
phrases.notes: The scarf

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 50 by showing that the two cases differ.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A shirt and a scarf are the same, so the scarf ruling covers the shirt.
steps.terutzMaskana: A shirt looks like whitening and a scarf does not, so the shirt needed a separate ruling.

steps.title: רב חסדא begins a statement about a linen shirt
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא opens a new statement about a linen shirt. It continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This linen shirt...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. רב חסדא starts a new ruling about a linen shirt, and the rest comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new teaching on the same item, the linen shirt. So far only the subject has been introduced. The ruling itself has not been stated yet.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
This linen shirt,
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement on the same topic of a linen shirt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. Only the subject, a linen shirt, has been introduced.
